subtype: Approach: deciding when to stop or hand over [Revision]
passage: “Lokesh, you asked how the handover happened, so here's the story. I ran the school events site for a year. In January I looked at my exam timetable and my to-do list, and I knew I couldn't do both. So I stopped adding features. I wrote a one-page note: how to add an event, where to find the photos, who to ask if something breaks, what not to touch. Then I gave it to you, and I put a banner across the top of the site: ‘Paused until April. New events will be added by Lokesh.’ It felt strange, almost like giving up a pet. But I'd rather say honestly it's paused than let it sit there quietly going out of date. — Payal

qa.q: What did Payal put across the top of the site?
qa.a: A banner saying it is paused until April, with new events added by Lokesh.

qa.q: How does Payal feel about handing over the site?
qa.a: Bittersweet: it felt like giving up a pet, but Payal was relieved not to let it go stale in silence.

qa.q: What else could Payal do to help the handover, and why?
qa.a: Do the first update together with Lokesh, since watching it done once makes the written notes easier to follow.

qa.q: How does the handover look to Lokesh?
qa.a: Lokesh receives a project with clear notes, though Lokesh may feel nervous about looking after something someone else built.

grounding: As board exams approach, a student freezes features, writes notes for a junior to maintain the site and pauses it honestly.

subtype: Approach: deciding when to stop or hand over [Revision]
passage:
I'm Jeevan, from Class Nine. I help with the school quiz site that Rehana built. In December she stopped adding things. She'd been planning a leaderboard, and I asked about it twice. Both times she said, “Not before boards.”
In January she sat with me in the library for three lunch breaks. She had a thin notebook: how to add a new quiz, how to fix the answer key, who to ask if the hosting stopped. She made me do each step while she watched, not the other way round.
Then she put a line on the home page: “Paused till April for board exams. New quizzes on Mondays only, by Jeevan.” I thought she'd feel sad about it. She looked relieved, if anything, but I can't really say.
It's March now. I've added six quizzes. Nobody has complained that the site looks dead.

qa.a: How to add a new quiz, how to fix the answer key, and who to ask if the hosting stopped.

qa.q: How did Rehana seem to feel after posting the pause notice?
qa.a: She looked relieved rather than sad, though Jeevan admits not being sure.

qa.q: What else could Rehana have done before pausing?
qa.a: Set a short monthly check-in with Jeevan, so questions don't pile up while the site is in someone else's hands.

qa.q: What is the handover like for Jeevan?
qa.a: Jeevan gets real responsibility and a clear notebook, having practised each step, so running the site feels manageable.

grounding: A junior sees a student freeze features before board exams, write short notes for a successor, and pause the site honestly.

subtype: Approach: deciding when to stop or hand over [Revision]
passage:
October 3: Ujjwal's cricket-scores site for the colony league has twelve teams, a points table and match reports. He has a list of eight features still to build. Boards are in February. Seema, his neighbour in Class Eight, asks when live scores are coming. “Soon,” he says, and feels his stomach tighten.
October 20: He opens the feature list and draws a line under it. No more features. He spends the evening writing four pages of notes: how to enter a score, how the table updates, what to do if a page breaks. He asks Seema to take over the match reports. She says yes, if he shows her first.
November 2: They sit together on the steps with the laptop while Seema adds a result herself. That night Ujjwal posts on the site: “Updates by Seema until March. I'll be back after boards.” Then he closes the laptop.

qa.q: How many features were still on Ujjwal's list on October 3?
What does Ujjwal's tight stomach on October 3 suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt anxious and a little guilty, promising "soon" while knowing boards left no time for eight more features.

qa.q: What else could Ujjwal do to make the pause clear to visitors?
qa.a: Add a note on the points table page too, saying when updates resume, so no one thinks the league site is abandoned.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Seema?
qa.a: Seema gets a clear role with notes and a practice session, which feels doable rather than being handed a site with no help.

grounding: Shows a student freezing features before board exams, writing notes for a junior to keep the site going, and announcing the pause honestly.
